description: For each rating, count the distinct film titles that have at least one copy in inventory; keep the ratings above the average count, then return the sum of their counts and their average amount above the average.

c.request: Looking at the films we have in stock by `rating`, which ratings have more films in inventory than the average rating does? Give me a single row with the total films in stock across those above-average ratings and, on average, how far above the across-rating average they are (no rounding). For each rating, count the distinct film titles that have at least one copy in inventory; keep the ratings above the average count, then return the sum of their counts and their average amount above the average.
c.sql: WITH rating_counts AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT f.film_id) AS film_count FROM film AS f JOIN inventory AS i ON i.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), rating_average AS (SELECT AVG(film_count) AS avg_film_count FROM rating_counts) SELECT SUM(rc.film_count) AS total_films_in_stock, AVG(rc.film_count - ra.avg_film_count) AS avg_above_rating_average FROM rating_counts AS rc CROSS JOIN rating_average AS ra WHERE rc.film_count > ra.avg_film_count;

b.request: For each rating, count distinct film titles with at least one inventory copy; select ratings whose counts exceed the average count across ratings, then return one row with the sum of the selected counts and the unrounded average amount by which those counts exceed the across-rating average
b.sql: WITH rating_counts AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT f.title) AS title_count FROM film AS f JOIN inventory AS i ON i.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), rating_average AS (SELECT AVG(title_count) AS avg_title_count FROM rating_counts) SELECT SUM(rc.title_count) AS selected_title_count_sum, AVG(rc.title_count - ra.avg_title_count) AS avg_excess FROM rating_counts AS rc CROSS JOIN rating_average AS ra WHERE rc.title_count > ra.avg_title_count

a.request: For each film `rating`, count the distinct films that have at least one copy in inventory (each title once, however many copies). Which ratings have more such films than the average of these counts across all ratings? Give one row with the total number of those films across those above-average ratings and the average amount by which their counts exceed the across-rating average, unrounded.
a.sql: WITH rating_counts AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT f.film_id) AS film_count FROM film AS f JOIN inventory AS i ON i.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), rating_average AS (SELECT AVG(film_count) AS avg_film_count FROM rating_counts) SELECT SUM(rc.film_count) AS total_films, AVG(rc.film_count - ra.avg_film_count) AS avg_excess FROM rating_counts AS rc CROSS JOIN rating_average AS ra WHERE rc.film_count > ra.avg_film_count

d.request: For each film rating, count the distinct film titles with at least one copy in inventory. Which ratings have counts above the average across ratings? Return a single row containing the sum of their counts and their average amount above that across-rating average, without rounding.
d.sql: WITH rating_counts AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT f.title) AS title_count FROM film AS f JOIN inventory AS i ON i.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), rating_average AS (SELECT AVG(title_count) AS avg_count FROM rating_counts) SELECT SUM(rc.title_count) AS total_titles, AVG(rc.title_count - ra.avg_count) AS avg_amount_above_average FROM rating_counts AS rc CROSS JOIN rating_average AS ra WHERE rc.title_count > ra.avg_count
